svg.title: What USPS pages say about return to sender, which they treat as three situations. 1, mail for someone else: for a previous resident or a person who does not live there, write "Not at this address" and give it to the carrier or a collection box, without erasing the address; for a piece delivered to the wrong location, write nothing and put it back or hand it to the carrier; for Priority Mail Express only, call 1-800-ASK-USPS; the FAQ says destroying mail not meant for you may be prohibited by law. 2, you refuse it: refuse it when offered, or after delivery mark it "Refused" and return it unopened within a reasonable time; an opened piece needs a new envelope, correct address and new postage; Registered, insured, Certified, COD and Adult Signature mail cannot be returned postage-free after delivery; accountable mail can be refused before signing by checking "Refused" on the notice. 3, you sent it: it goes to the return address; with none, the local Post Office or the Mail Recovery Center handles it; Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, First-Class Mail and USPS Ground Advantage are returned at no additional charge unless the sender asks otherwise; USPS Marketing Mail is not returned unless endorsed; if it has not arrived in 7 days, use Missing Mail. Where the pages differ: the refusal FAQ cites DMM 604.8.1.2 and 507.1.8.2 but the refusal text is in DMM 508.1.1; the FAQ's not-refusable list has four types and the DMM adds Adult Signature; a reasonable time is not defined; the pages do not say whether "Not at this address" mail must be unopened. Sources: USPS FAQs 000006175 and 000006162 and DMM 507, 508 and 604, read Nov. 20, 2026.
